findings.title: One GitHub call per pull request, and a whole job log downloaded for each failing check
findings.evidence: ci-watch calls gh pr checks once per open pull request (line 56, inside the loop at line 88), and isGateFailure then downloads the complete log of every failing check with gh run view --log (line 77) to look for one line in it. That is the shape PERF-01 describes: work per row rather than per call. Three things bound the harm rather than removing it — gh exposes no batch endpoint for checks, so the per-pull-request call is forced; the row count is open pull requests, two today and realistically under twenty for this repository; and this is dev tooling run from a terminal or a 60-second monitor, not a request path with a user waiting. The log download is the real cost, since a log is far larger than the one line read from it.
findings.fix: If it ever drags, GitHub's GraphQL API returns statusCheckRollup for many pull requests in a single call, which removes the per-pull-request query entirely. For the log, gh run view --log --job already narrows to one job; narrowing further is not possible, so the cheaper route is to cache the gate answer per job id for the life of the process, since the same failing job is re-read on every poll.

summary: Pass, with 1 medium finding open and 1 fixed. PERF-01 stands: one GitHub call per pull request and a full job log per failing check — forced by gh, bounded by open pull request count, but the shape the rule names. TEST-01 is fixed: the scripts were made importable, and the ERROR-on-failure, wrong-shape and keep-going paths are now asserted with a fake runner. No serious problem.
